title: Maximum Coins From K Consecutive Bags
statement:
A number line has one bag at every integer position. `coins` describes the bags that are not empty: `coins[i] = [l_i, r_i, c_i]` means each bag at a position from `l_i` to `r_i` (both included) holds `c_i` coins. These segments never overlap and may be listed in any order; every bag outside them holds nothing.

You may take `k` bags whose positions are consecutive and keep all of their coins. Return the largest number of coins you can get.
notes:
## Intuition

Positions reach 10^9, so trying every start is hopeless. Shifting a window one step right swaps its first bag for the bag after its end; shifting it left does the reverse. Unless the window starts at some `l_i` or ends at some `r_i`, one of the two shifts loses nothing, and repeating it brings an end onto such a boundary. So only the 2n windows that start at an `l_i` or end at an `r_i` matter.

Windows ending at a right end can be swept with a variable-size window over the sorted segments. Windows starting at a left end are the same thing in a mirror: map `[l, r]` to `[-r, -l]` and sweep again.

## Approach

1. `rightAligned` sorts the segments by start. Each segment's `end` in turn is the window's last bag, so the window starts at `windowStart = end - k + 1`.
2. Add that segment's coins to `cover`, the full coins of segments `left` through the current one.
3. While segment `left` ends before `windowStart`, take its coins out and advance `left`.
4. The bags of segment `left` before `windowStart` are `outside` the window, so the window holds `cover - outside`. Keep the best.
5. Sweep `mirrored` the same way and return the larger result.

## Example 1, step by step

Sorted, the segments are `[1,3,2]`, `[5,6,4]`, `[8,10,1]`, with `k = 4`. The window ending at 3 holds 6. The window ending at 6 starts at 3: `cover = 6 + 8 = 14`, minus `outside = 4` for bags 1 and 2, gives 10. The window ending at 10 starts at 7, so both earlier segments leave and it holds 3. The mirrored sweep checks the windows starting at 8, 5 and 1, worth 3, 9 and 6. The answer is `10`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) for sorting; each sweep is O(n) because `left` only moves forward.
- Space: O(n) for the mirrored copy.

## Pitfalls

- Windows that start at an `l_i` alone miss Example 1's best window, bags 3 to 6, which ends at `r = 6`.
- A window may hold only part of a segment (Example 2 takes 2 of its 10 bags).
- The segments arrive unsorted.
- The answer can reach 10^12, so Java and C need 64-bit integers.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `rightAligned` | best total over windows that end at some segment's right end |
| `start`, `end`, `count` | the current segment: first bag, last bag, coins per bag |
| `windowStart` | the window's first bag, `end - k + 1` |
| `cover` | coins of segments `left` through the current one, in full |
| `left` | the first segment that still reaches the window |
| `outside` | coins of segment `left` that lie before `windowStart` |
| `best` | the best window total so far |
| `mirrored` | the segments reflected, so starts at `l_i` become right ends |

narration.3: rightAligned tries every window whose last bag is the right end of a segment.
narration.4: Sort the segments by their left end so the window can sweep them in order.
narration.6: cover holds the coins of every segment from left to the current one, counted in full.
narration.7: left is the first segment that may still reach into the window.
narration.8: Each segment's right end becomes the window's last bag in turn.
narration.9: The current segment ends where the window ends, so count all of its coins for now; any part before the window is taken off below.
narration.10: A window of k bags that ends at end starts at end - k + 1.
narration.11: Does segment left end before the window starts?
narration.12: Then none of its bags are in the window: take all of its coins back out.
narration.13: Move on to the next segment.
narration.15: Segment left may begin before the window; these are the coins of its bags that fall outside.
narration.16: The window holds cover minus those outside coins; keep the best total.
narration.18: This is the best window among those ending at a right end.
narration.22: Reflect every segment, [l, r] to [-r, -l], so a window starting at l becomes one ending at -l.
narration.23: Sweep both versions and return the better total.
